method: Research review of 62 historical actions and original Weiser page images. 61 indexed pages or adjacent claim pages were successfully opened; the remaining image (printed p131) failed and is kept on hold. Exact source-label conflicts also remain held. Source action review is not approval of distinct Catholic custom identities.
precautions: This registry does not imply full-page line-by-line certification or modern community continuity.
Source-specific liturgy, disciplinary laws and historical Eastern usage are not presumed to govern current Roman 1962 Calendar.
Current indulgence laws cannot be inferred from 1958 descriptions or superficial name matching.
Further non-Weiser witnesses and EN/FR editorial approval required before publishing.
Printed page 131 repeatedly failed retrieval; it has NOT been visually checked. Its label and identity are not certified.

records.label_from_index: Easter open house and family visits
records.narrow_evidence_en: Easter Sunday household open-house visits, family meals and social hospitality documented as regional seasonal custom.

records.label_from_index: Easter egg hunt traditions
records.narrow_evidence_en: Easter egg hunting and egg games are family customs, not indulgenced works merely by taking place at Easter.

records.label_from_index: Sign of the Cross during ordinary household work on Trinity Sunday
records.narrow_evidence_en: Devotional sign of Cross in household work on Trinity Sunday appears as voluntary domestic sign, not an imposed new feast gesture.

records.label_from_index: Reliquary shrine relic-veneration observances
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historically displayed reliquaries, official veneration and feast days at shrines; rituals require legitimate authority.

records.label_from_index: Annunciation image placed among seed grain with prayer
records.narrow_evidence_en: Central European farmer places Annunciation image in seed-grain container while praying to Mary; weather-protection belief not guaranteed.

records.label_from_index: Saint Patrick's Breastplate prayer observance
records.narrow_evidence_en: Saint Patrick's Breastplate (Lorica) used as Irish morning devotion; the historical author of the text remains uncertain.

records.label_from_index: Saint Lucy white-robed bride and candle wreath breakfast
records.narrow_evidence_en: Scandinavian girl dressed in white wearing Saint Lucy candle wreath serves family coffee/cakes December 13; do not conflate with witchcraft folklore.

records.label_from_index: Named family member lights Christmas candles
records.narrow_evidence_en: Original printed p131 screenshot could not be retrieved after multiple attempts; neighbouring p130 discusses family Advent candle lighting but does not certify the exact named-family-member Christmas-candle claim.

records.label_from_index: Voluntary Septuagesima preparatory fasting
records.narrow_evidence_en: Voluntary Septuagesima fast as preparation for Lent; not an obligatory fasting rule.

records.label_from_index: Hooded Holy Week confraternity processions
records.narrow_evidence_en: Hooded penitential Holy Week confraternities and outdoor processions in Spain and Latin America, geographically contingent.

records.label_from_index: Te Deum at local thanksgiving liturgy
records.narrow_evidence_en: Te Deum at extraordinary public thanksgiving with Mass or Benediction, historically attested; not evidence by itself of a New Year Te Deum concession.

records.label_from_index: Pilgrimages to grain-robed Marian images
records.narrow_evidence_en: The page cited for a grain-robed Marian pilgrimage instead discusses other Assumption lore; a direct passage for that specific claim was not found.

records.label_from_index: Breton overnight prayer bells and farmhouse visits
records.narrow_evidence_en: Breton All Saints night men ring bells at farmhouses to call prayer for souls of the dead; regional and voluntary.

records.label_from_index: Croagh Patrick and Lough Derg penitential pilgrimages
records.narrow_evidence_en: Pilgrimage and penitential practices at Croagh Patrick and Lough Derg in Ireland, no automatic date or shrine-indulgence claim.

records.label_from_index: Valencia Fallas associated with Saint Joseph
records.narrow_evidence_en: Valencia Fallas bonfires, wood figures, carpenters' civic celebrations around Saint Joseph March 19, containing both devotional and secular features.

records.label_from_index: Traditional Christmas Eve fasting
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical vigil abstinence on Christmas Eve, distinguished from 1962 local discipline and contemporary law.

records.label_from_index: Epiphany proclamation of movable feasts
records.narrow_evidence_en: Epiphany proclamation of Easter and dependent movable feasts in church, a historically described ceremonial, not a new lay custom.

records.label_from_index: Irish Lenten matchmaking
records.narrow_evidence_en: Printed page 186 contains source references, not a direct description of Irish Lenten matchmaking; earlier p185 contains Laetare betrothal reference, but national attribution remains unverified.

records.label_from_index: Historical rulers' Mandatum foot washing and feeding the poor
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical rulers participated in Mandatum foot washing and almsgiving, unlike obligatory Roman Holy Thursday ritual.

records.label_from_index: French tale of bells flying to Rome at Easter
records.narrow_evidence_en: French Easter children's story that church bells fly to Rome and return with sweets is folktale, not a claim about real angels.

records.label_from_index: Moosburg Ascension dramatic apostles and angels
records.narrow_evidence_en: Moosburg Bavarian Ascension mystery pageant with simulated Apostles and angels, historical and not authorised universal Roman ritual.

records.label_from_index: Ascension flower and wafer shower at parish pageant
records.narrow_evidence_en: Ascension church play shower of flowers and communion wafers in medieval Bavaria; no contemporary Mass authorisation.

records.label_from_index: Medieval Corpus Christi mystery plays
records.narrow_evidence_en: Medieval Corpus Christi dramatic biblical plays, later restricted, not a universal approved Mass function.

records.label_from_index: Dragon, Saint George and masked figures in older Corpus Christi pageants
records.narrow_evidence_en: Dragon, Saint George, giant and mask figures in historical Corpus Christi festivities are popular pageantry, not inherently Eucharistic rites.

records.label_from_index: Candlemas rent-paying and farmhand move-day
records.narrow_evidence_en: Candlemas rent collection and hiring/moving date for farmworkers are local seasonal economic practices.

records.label_from_index: Giving saints' names at baptism
records.narrow_evidence_en: Naming a child for a saint at baptism as historic Catholic practice; name choice is not distinct from Baptism itself.

records.label_from_index: Ember seasonal quarter-term payment of debts and tithes
records.narrow_evidence_en: Ember quarter days associated in parts of Europe with paying rents, debts, harvest dues and tithes; secular quarter term not a universal devotional obligation.

records.label_from_index: Feast of the Ass ceremonial dramatization
records.narrow_evidence_en: Feast of the Ass dramatic church ceremonial and its subsequent suppression; not an authorised contemporary Mass rubric.

records.label_from_index: Historic Lenten prohibition of dairy and eggs
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical Lenten abstention from eggs and dairy in addition to flesh meat; no inference to current discipline.

records.label_from_index: Almsgiving connected to Lenten dairy dispensations
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historically, bishops granted Lenten dairy dispensations with charitable contributions to churches and charitable works; not an indulgence for payment.

records.label_from_index: Lenten and Passion hymn singing in community
records.narrow_evidence_en: Community Passion hymns and penitential singing in Lent attested; no claim of a specific approved Mass chant interpolation.

records.label_from_index: Restriction of social entertainment and dances during Lent
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical Lent avoidance of secular entertainment and dancing by local custom, distinct from binding universal fasting law.

records.label_from_index: Passion oratorios and devotional dramas during Lent
records.narrow_evidence_en: Concerts and oratorios on Passion themes, especially in German-speaking lands, are devotional arts rather than Mass rites.

records.label_from_index: Easter prisoner release or public reconciliation custom
records.narrow_evidence_en: Royal liberation of prisoners and local reconciliation on Easter historically reported, not a church liturgical duty.

records.label_from_index: Medieval elevation of image from Holy Sepulchre at Easter
records.narrow_evidence_en: Medieval Holy Sepulchre image-lifting or cross ceremony during Easter drama, distinct from Roman Mass order.

records.label_from_index: Visitatio sepulcri medieval Easter church drama
records.narrow_evidence_en: Medieval Visitatio sepulcri dramatic visit to the tomb with choir dialogues, historically described, not current universal rite.

records.label_from_index: O filii et filiae sung during Easter
records.narrow_evidence_en: Index page 230 describes Easter hymns generally; O filii et filiae title not confirmed on examined leaf; earlier title citation required.

records.label_from_index: Easter oratorio performances and concerts
records.narrow_evidence_en: Easter oratorios or concerts as artistic devotional celebrations, separate from Holy Mass and Office.

records.label_from_index: Annunciation or Lady Day marking legal New Year
records.narrow_evidence_en: Annunciation or Lady Day used as legal New Year in historical papal and English documents, no longer current civil calendar.

records.label_from_index: Lenten parish mission before Easter Confession
records.narrow_evidence_en: Lenten parish missions, Confession and reconciliation before Easter documented in Latin-country parish practice.

records.label_from_index: Historical Palm Sunday donkey-image procession
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical Palm Sunday donkey-image processions and Passion representation, distinct from approved Roman procession rubrics.

records.label_from_index: Early Irish missionary blessed Easter bonfire tradition
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical Irish Paschal fire attributed to early missionaries and later Easter Vigil fire customs; avoid uncertain attribution as fact.

records.label_from_index: Historical Ascension walking procession recalling Bethany
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historic Ascension walking from town to fields recalling Mount of Olives and Bethany; local seasonal procession, not a universal rubric.

records.label_from_index: Adoration as Corpus Christi procession passes a home
records.narrow_evidence_en: Household adoration as a Corpus Christi Eucharistic procession passes, distinct from decorating a route and from personally joining procession.

records.label_from_index: Corpus Christi roadside stations and Benediction
records.narrow_evidence_en: Corpus Christi processional stations for Benediction, historically local ritual disposition rather than required number of stops.

records.label_from_index: Hanging blessed Corpus Christi wreaths at home or by fields
records.narrow_evidence_en: Polish priests bless Corpus Christi flower wreaths, hung later in homes and fields; source passage begins on p265 rather than indexed reference p266.

records.label_from_index: Polish harvest wreaths presented for blessing
records.narrow_evidence_en: Harvest-wreath processions and priestly blessing in Polish rural parishes, tied to local harvest occasions.

records.label_from_index: Historical Candlemas cemetery procession
records.narrow_evidence_en: Old Candlemas procession formerly traversing churchyard past graves before changing to church-only, not a current cemetery procession.

records.label_from_index: Priestly grave blessing on All Souls
records.narrow_evidence_en: Historical priest blessing graves on All Souls with holy water amid processions and prayers, linked to cemetery observance.

records.label_from_index: Family reconciliation before Russian Easter confession
records.narrow_evidence_en: Russian households reconcile before pre-Easter Confession; described in Eastern context, not universal 1962 Latin custom.

records.label_from_index: Historical priestly blessing of Easter eggs
records.narrow_evidence_en: Priestly blessing of Easter eggs in some communities; distinct from egg gifting, games and foods.

records.label_from_index: Historical priestly blessing of Easter ham
records.narrow_evidence_en: A historical blessing for Easter ham or meat before a family meal is described; not a universally mandated 1962 Easter rite.

records.label_from_index: Gathering and presenting St John herbs for blessing
records.narrow_evidence_en: Saint John's Eve herbs are gathered and blessed where local clergy actually perform blessing; no universal medicinal guarantee.

records.label_from_index: Historic Lenten catechumen instruction and preparation
records.narrow_evidence_en: Early-church Lent catechumen instruction and scrutinies, distinct from later 1962 or modern catechetical rites.

records.label_from_index: Public penitents ritually reconciled on Holy Thursday
records.narrow_evidence_en: Public penitents ritually reconciled on Holy Thursday in historical church discipline, not general current sacramental absolution.

records.label_from_index: Older Holy Thursday altar-washing ceremony
records.narrow_evidence_en: Former Holy Thursday ceremonial washing of altars and church furniture, not current 1962 Mass action.

records.label_from_index: Byzantine midnight Easter Resurrection procession
records.narrow_evidence_en: Byzantine midnight Resurrection procession and greeting follows Eastern rite, not 1962 Roman Easter Vigil rubrics.

records.label_from_index: Historical Pentecost Vigil baptism and font blessing
records.narrow_evidence_en: Earlier Latin Pentecost Vigil baptism and font blessing rites, many historically discontinued, not simply copied into the 1962 rite.

records.label_from_index: Eastern Saturday of Souls kollyba blessing and grave visits
records.narrow_evidence_en: Byzantine Saturday of Souls prayers, kollyba blessing and cemetery visit before Pentecost, distinct from Latin calendar.

records.label_from_index: Polish Gromniczna candle and wolf/thunder folklore
records.narrow_evidence_en: Polish Candlemas thunder-candle and wolf legend is folklore; protection claims should not be asserted.

records.label_from_index: Saint John bonfire straw effigies and noisy demon-averting folklore
records.narrow_evidence_en: Saint John bonfire effigies, noise to repel demons and allegedly protective effects are treated as folklore, distinct from prayers and hymns.

records.label_from_index: Western European local Easter folk hymns
records.narrow_evidence_en: Several local English/French Easter hymns and folk songs are listed outside the official Mass Proper.
